_about: The unit record: what every data/units/<id>.json carries. scripts/sim/unit_def.gd VALIDATES EACH FILE AGAINST THIS at load: a field listed here and missing from a file is a load error, never a default; a field in a file and not listed here is a load error too (it catches a misspelt key that would otherwise be ignored). Files starting with '_' are not units. The SHAPE is PROPOSED by Track S, 2026-10-09; the design doc's unit design sheet (Execution plan > Design work > Unit design sheets) lists what a full sheet holds, and the fields not here yet (weapons, engagement parameters, specials, armor, shadow behaviour, card contents) come with combat and the unit sheets.

conventions.units: Metres, seconds, metres per second, metres per second squared. Angles are DEGREES in data and radians at runtime (unit_def.gd converts).
conventions.frame: World x to the right, y DOWN (the prototype's canvas and Godot 2D). A heading of 0 points along +x; a positive turn is clockwise on screen (a right turn); the direction of motion is Vector2(cos(heading), sin(heading)).
conventions.value_record: Every tunable is a value record. While it is a placeholder: {"value": v, "_proposed": true, "_reason": "one line"}. Once a variant board or Alex sets it: {"value": v, "decision": "<id in data/decisions/decisions.json>"}. A record with neither is a load error, so no number can enter the game without saying where it came from (working rules 2 and 3). Plain fields (kind text or enum) are identity, not tuning, and are not records.
conventions.keys_starting_with_underscore: Comments. Allowed anywhere, ignored by the loader.

kinds.number: a value record holding a number >= 'min' (and <= 'max' where given)
kinds.integer: a value record holding a whole number >= 'min'
kinds.bool: a value record holding true or false
kinds.curve: a value record holding [[speed_mps, value], ...]: at least one point, speeds strictly increasing, values >= 0. Read by straight-line interpolation between points and held flat beyond the first and last point.
kinds.band_list: a value record holding a non-empty list of band ids from data/sim/altitude.json, no repeats
kinds.band: a value record holding one band id from data/sim/altitude.json
kinds.section: an object whose own fields are listed under 'fields'

id.about: Unit type id; must equal the file name without .json. The World's units refer to it as their 'type'.

name.about: Display name, from the design doc's Initial unit roster.

domain.about: From the Initial unit roster table.

size_m.about: Largest planform dimension: wingspan for aircraft, length for tanks and ships. Drawing scale and, later, hit size.

actions_per_turn.about: Steps per turn: the number of points on the unit's motion curve each turn. data/sim/turn.json splits turn_seconds into this many equal steps.

health.about: Hit points; the unit card's pips. Carried, unused until combat.

sight_range_m.about: Vision radius for fog of war. Carried, unused until Track F's first vision rule reads it.

drawing.about: How the unit is drawn. Carried, unused by the simulation.

silhouette.about: Silhouette id for the drawing layer; chosen from a variant board (design doc, Unit design sheets).

envelope.about: The performance envelope (scripts/sim/envelope.gd). Each step the player picks a point; the envelope decides which points are reachable from the unit's state at the start of the step. Inertia: speed changes at most accel/decel per second, heading at most the turn rate at the step's starting speed, and turning and climbing cost speed.

speed_min_mps.about: Slowest the unit flies or moves. Aircraft: stall speed (a plane never falls below it from above it; no stall rule yet). Ground and sea: 0, or negative for the fastest reverse.

speed_cruise_mps.about: The unit's normal speed: where a new unit starts unless placed otherwise, and what the dumb AI flies at.

speed_max_mps.about: Top speed in level flight or on the level.

dive_speed_max_mps.about: Never-exceed speed: a dive may carry the unit past speed_max_mps up to this; above speed_max it then sheds speed at its full deceleration. Equal to speed_max_mps for units that cannot dive.

accel_mps2.about: Largest speed GAIN per second at full power. Per step it is accel x step_dt -- a rate, not a per-step figure, so a change to turn length or actions per turn does not silently change how hard a unit accelerates.

decel_mps2.about: Largest speed LOSS per second (throttle back, drag, brakes).

reverse_from_stop.about: Ships and tanks: true means speed cannot cross zero within a step; the unit must come to a stop, then may reverse (design doc, Motion and inertia: ships can reverse once stopped). Aircraft: false.

turn_rate_curve_dps.about: Largest heading change per second as a function of the speed at the start of the step (absolute speed when reversing). Planes: high at low speed, low at high speed (a tighter turn when slow). Ships: 0 at 0 speed, rising with way on (a rudder needs flow). Tanks: one flat point (pivot steering).

turn_bleed_mps2.about: Speed lost per second while turning at the full available rate, subtracted from both ends of the step's speed window. Planes lose speed in turns (design doc, Motion and inertia).

turn_bleed_exponent.about: Bleed for a partial turn is turn_bleed_mps2 x (turn used / turn available)^exponent. 2 tracks induced drag, which grows with the square of the load factor: gentle turns are nearly free, hard turns bite.

altitude_bands.about: The bands this unit may occupy, from data/sim/altitude.json. Aircraft: air bands. Ground and sea: ["surface"].

start_band.about: Band a new unit starts in unless placed otherwise; must be one of altitude_bands.

bands_per_step.about: Most bands the unit may climb or dive in one step. 0 for units that cannot change band.

climb_speed_cost_mps.about: Speed lost per band climbed in a step. A climb the unit cannot afford without falling below speed_min_mps is refused (the band stays).

dive_speed_gain_mps.about: Speed gained per band dived in a step; diving adds speed (design doc, Height). May carry the unit up to dive_speed_max_mps.
